notes:
Summary: SMB, early discovery. Small CX startup building an in-app AI assistant + internal knowledge search. Primary interest: Redwood Hosted API (self-serve) because they want minimal ops and quick time-to-value.

Key requirements / pain: 
- Workload: real-time chat widget (concurrent users during promotions) + embeddings for doc search. Expect periodic traffic spikes (marketing emails -> 300-500 concurrent widget requests for 2-10 minutes).
- Latency target: P95 < 300ms for assistant responses; will accept slightly higher for embedding batch jobs.
- Throughput: baseline ~20 reqs/s, peak bursts up to ~350 reqs/s during campaigns.
- Cost sensitivity: medium — need predictable unit costs, want guidance to avoid runaway token spend.
- Model preference: small/medium open models for chat (cost/latency tradeoff), fallback to a cheaper distilled variant on overload.
- Routing/fallback: want automatic fallback to lower-cost model on 429s or capacity limits; interested in per-route quotas.
- Rate-limiting specifics asked: how Redwood surfaces 429s, Retry-After header semantics, per-key concurrency limits vs global account quotas, and burst allowance windows.
- Desired SDK behavior: recommended exponential backoff + full jitter; client-side concurrency semaphore example for Node/Browser; sample code requested.
- Observability: needs per-key token usage, per-route latency and 429 counts; wants alerts when 429 rate >1% over 5m.
- Security/compliance: SSO + audit logs required for enterprise features in future; currently public cloud ok but retention controls should be available.

Direct quotes: 
- "We can't have the chat widget go dark for 5 minutes during a campaign — graceful degrade is a must." — R. Walsh, VP Eng
- "If we get a steady trickle of 429s it's a blocker for launch; we need clear retry semantics and sample client code." — S. Kim, Lead FE

POC ask: 
- Provide a hosted API quota profile that supports burst windows (e.g., baseline QPS 20, burst bucket 500 for up to 120 seconds), and sample backoff strategy.
- Short checklist for integrating SDK concurrency controls + guidance on token batching/streaming to reduce token count.
- Example alert rule for console to detect rate-limit pressure.

2) Schedule 30m technical deep-dive w/ Maya and R. Walsh wk of Mar 15 to review POC config and monitoring.
